summary: Intro discovery for Bluehaven Capital evaluating Redwood Dedicated. Covered current stack, isolation needs, expected QPS, burst strategy, security/compliance concerns (SOC 2, KMS, audit logs), and next steps for pricing, benchmarks and a technical deep dive.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-17 14:00 PST | Duration 50m | Attendees: Samir Patel, Lena Ortiz (Redwood); Evan Park, Marisol Gomez, Derek Liu, Priya Shah (Bluehaven)

Summary: Quick discovery to understand Bluehaven's needs for a Dedicated GPU pool, isolation and burst behavior, expected workloads and compliance asks. Agreed to follow up with pricing, security docs and a benchmark plan.

[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, I'm the AE on this; with me is Lena Ortiz, our solutions engineer. How are you all doing?
[00:08] Evan Park: Good thanks, yeah excited to dive in.
[00:12] Marisol Gomez: Hey all, Marisol here. We're trying to get a sense of options — hosted vs dedicated vs private — but today's mostly focused on dedicated.
[00:20] Lena Ortiz: Great, we'll focus on dedicated: reserved GPU pools, isolation, burst policies. Quick ask: can you share current model sizes and expected QPS?
[00:28] Priya Shah: Yeah, quick context: we run a mix of transformer models, mainly 7B and 13B variants, a couple of custom fine-tuned models for summarization and routing. Expected baseline qps is 15-20 requests/sec with spikes to ~120 qps during morning hours.
[00:45] Derek Liu: From security side, we need strong isolation, audit logs, KMS support — and we will need SOC 2 evidence.
[00:53] Samir Patel: That's helpful. For Dedicated, we provide isolated GPU pools — you can reserve capacity (e.g., 4x A100) and configure burst to additional nodes. Autoscale can be configured but typically for strict isolation customers prefer pre-warmed burst nodes.
[01:12] Evan Park: When you say burst, is that across the same tenant or multi-tenant fallback? We prefer not to hit shared pool.
[01:20] Lena Ortiz: Good question — you can set policies: strict (no shared fallback) or graceful (fallback to compatible model variants in shared capacity). For compliance-sensitive customers we recommend strict with configured burst reserve we provision for you.
[01:35] Marisol Gomez: And pricing for strict burst — is that charged as reserved or pay-as-you-burst?
[01:41] Samir Patel: Typically reserved for baseline and a burst buffer as reserved commit for predictable billing; we can do a hybrid: reserved baseline + billed on usage for temporary burst. We'll send detailed pricing variations.
[01:55] Priya Shah: Network wise, we need VPC peering and customer-managed subnets, plus control plane access restrictions. Can Redwood support VPC-only control plane?
[02:05] Lena Ortiz: We offer a private control plane option for Dedicated customers — customer-managed VPC, or Private (on-prem) if required. For Dedicated in a cloud region we can give VPC peering and strict egress rules; the control plane endpoints can be locked down via IP allowlist and SAML SSO.
[02:20] Derek Liu: Encryption at rest: must be customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Does Redwood integrate with external KMS?
[02:26] Samir Patel: Yes, we support AWS KMS and external HSM integrations for key management. We'll attach our SOC 2 appendix and KMS integration guide.
[02:36] Evan Park: On performance — we saw claims around batching and KV cache. For our long context prompts (up to 4k tokens) what kind of latency should we target?
[02:45] Lena Ortiz: Latency depends on model size, quantization and batching. For a 13B model on A100 80GB with optimized kernels and continuous batching, median p50 generation latencies for 1k tokens is typically in the 300-600ms range; p95 varies more. We'll propose sample profiles once we see your seq length distribution.
[03:05] Marisol Gomez: Our main concern is tail latencies during spikes. How does Redwood handle queueing vs dropping requests?
[03:12] Samir Patel: You can set concurrency limits per route and define fallback policies — e.g., route to a smaller quantized variant, or return a graceful degradation message. We also support token-level caching to cut costs and latency for repeated prefixes.
[03:28] Priya Shah: On the dedicated nodes, is there any noisy neighbor risk if we run other customers' workloads?
[03:33] Lena Ortiz: No noisy neighbor on a dedicated pool — compute and memory are isolated. Shared fallback is separate; that is only if you allow it.
[03:40] Evan Park: Ok that helps. Can you explain the typical sizing guidance? We have 20 baseline qps, 120 peak. Models are 7B (~13B after tokenizer expansion).
[03:50] Lena Ortiz: Rough ballpark: for synchronous generation 7B you can expect ~x tokens/sec per A100 v100/80GB. For 20 qps work with short responses, 1-2 nodes might be fine; for 120 qps peaks, we suggest a baseline of 2-4 reserved nodes plus a 2-node burst buffer or autoscale target. We'll run a sizing calc during the tech deep dive.
[04:12] Marisol Gomez: We also run embeddings for search on daytime hours — that's heavy throughput but lower latency constraints. Can Dedicated pool be multi-purpose?
[04:20] Samir Patel: Yes, you can carve routes with tags to target different node types; embedding workloads can be routed to separate instance types optimized for throughput. You can reserve capacity for embeddings separately to avoid interference.
[04:32] Derek Liu: Compliance question: can we get complete audit logs of requests, redaction options, and retention policies?
[04:38] Lena Ortiz: Audit logs are available — token-level logs can be turned off or redacted; retention configurable per contract. We'll include the audit log doc.
[04:47] Priya Shah: Network egress: any traffic leaving our VPC must be logged and pass through our firewall. Can Redwood accommodate that?
[04:53] Samir Patel: Yes, we can support VPC peering and keep data flow internal; for stricter needs we have a private deployment option where control plane sits in your network.
[05:02] Evan Park: On model versions: we want to pin versions and do canary rollouts. Is that supported on Dedicated?
[05:09] Lena Ortiz: Absolutely — rollouts, A/B and canary with automatic fallback policies are supported. You can pin by model version or rollback to previous blob.
[05:18] Marisol Gomez: Do you support quantized variants for cost savings? We may want int8 for some routes.
[05:23] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we recommend quantized variants for cost/perf. We have verified quant profiles per model; you'll get recommendations from our Optimize toolkit after the initial workload analysis.
[05:33] Evan Park: Any limitations on model licensing — we use a mix of open models and some licensed third-party models.
[05:40] Samir Patel: Licensed models are fine as long as you have rights; we can host any customer-owned model in Dedicated or Private. We'll note any extra compliance steps if needed.
[05:50] Derek Liu: Regarding backups and snapshots of model artifacts — where are those stored and with what controls?
[05:56] Lena Ortiz: Models can live in your S3 (or equivalent) and our runtime pulls on deploy. Backups are under your account, and access is controlled via IAM. For strict data residency we can arrange regional storage.
[06:09] Evan Park: Ok, shifting to benchmarks: we'd like a 48-hour pilot with our typical inference mix to validate throughput and p95 latency. Is that common?
[06:17] Lena Ortiz: Yes — we often do 48-72 hour pilots. We provision a small Dedicated pool and run your traces; we instrument cost/latency and produce a benchmark report. We'll need your traces, model artifacts and an access window.
[06:27] Marisol Gomez: Who manages the pilot infra — Redwood or our cloud team?
[06:31] Samir Patel: Redwood manages the Dedicated infra for Hosted/Dedicated. For Private/on-prem customers, your infra team manages deployment with our package. For the pilot we'll provision in our managed Dedicated in your chosen region.
[06:44] Priya Shah: Any SLA targets for Dedicated? We have strict uptime needs for the trading desk.
[06:49] Samir Patel: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime for the reserved pool; we can discuss specific numbers in contracting. Typically 99.9% or better depending on commitment level.
[06:59] Evan Park: Integration with our identity provider? We use Okta.
[07:03] Lena Ortiz: We support SAML SSO/SCIM and RBAC; Okta is a common integration.
[07:09] Derek Liu: Will Redwood maintain separate admin planes for different business units? We have multiple teams and need per-team RBAC and billing separation.
[07:16] Samir Patel: Yes — role-based access, org units and per-route billing are supported. We'll show examples in the console during the deep dive.
[07:26] Marisol Gomez: On capacity planning — can you provide a couple of scenarios: conservative (no shared fallback) vs cost-optimized (shared fallback)?
[07:33] Lena Ortiz: We'll prepare two capacity plans: conservative (fully reserved, separate burst nodes) and cost-optimized (smaller reserved + shared fallback to compatible quantized models).
[07:43] Evan Park: How long does provisioning take when we order dedicated nodes?
[07:47] Samir Patel: Provisioning a Dedicated pool is typically 24-72 hours depending on region and GPU availability; for large reserved contracts we can pre-book capacity.
[07:58] Priya Shah: We may need to run some initial load tests against our models — what's your recommended test harness?
[08:04] Lena Ortiz: We'll provide a benchmark harness and a spreadsheet template for traces and expected distributions. We also support running your JMeter/Locust traces against the pool.
[08:13] Marisol Gomez: Are there rate limits or quotas we should be aware of for Dedicated?
[08:18] Samir Patel: Limits are configurable per route; by default Dedicated pools have higher quotas but you can configure strict TPS and token limits.
[08:28] Evan Park: A question about billing granularity: do you bill per node-hour or per-token for Dedicated?
[08:33] Samir Patel: Reserved capacity is usually node-hour/commit-based; we can hybrid charge per-token for overflow/burst usage. We'll include example math in the pricing doc.
[08:45] Derek Liu: From a legal/procurement perspective we'll need the standard DPA and security annex. Who handles that?
[08:50] Samir Patel: Our legal ops will share the DPA, SOC 2 report and security annex. I'll attach those to the follow-up email.
[08:58] Priya Shah: Is there telemetry we can ingest — e.g., Prometheus metrics or traces into our observability stack?
[09:04] Lena Ortiz: Yes — Redwood Console exports metrics, and we can provide Prometheus endpoints or push metrics to common backends for retention.
[09:12] Evan Park: Great. For the pilot, what artifacts do you need from us?
[09:16] Lena Ortiz: We'll need: model artifacts (weights or access details), sample traffic traces with token distributions, desired seq lengths, and network/VPC constraints. Also a POA for access.
[09:25] Marisol Gomez: Timeline-wise, we're targeting a production decision by mid-December. Is that feasible?
[09:29] Samir Patel: Yes — pilot + evaluation in late Nov could align to a contract in early-december. We'll prioritize your pilot once we get artifacts.
[09:36] Evan Park: Any red flags on your side about our described workloads?
[09:39] Lena Ortiz: Nothing major; the peak spikes are the main dimension — we just need to size burst and concurrency carefully. Also, embedding throughput might need a separate capacity plan.
[09:49] Derek Liu: On data residency — some clients require EU-only regions; we need to set region requirements per dataset. Do you support region pinning?
[09:57] Samir Patel: Yes, you can pin deployments to a specific region and ensure logs and artifacts stay there.
[10:03] Priya Shah: Networking question: do we need to open any inbound ports to your control plane?
[10:07] Lena Ortiz: Usually we require outbound connections from your VPC to the control plane endpoints; we can set up private links if required for stricter environments.
[10:15] Evan Park: Could you walk briefly through an example allocation? Say 4x A100 baseline + 2-node burst?
[10:21] Lena Ortiz: Sure — baseline 4x A100 provides N concurrent generations depending on model; burst adds 2 additional A100s that autoscale up when average CPU/GPU utilization hits a threshold for X minutes. Billing model: baseline reserved monthly, burst billed per-hour or as reserved buffer.
[10:37] Marisol Gomez: Are there any costs associated with model downloads or staging?
[10:42] Samir Patel: There may be storage egress or staging fees if transferring large artifacts across regions; we'll call that out in the pricing doc.
[10:50] Derek Liu: For assurance, will we have a named technical contact at Redwood during pilot?
[10:55] Samir Patel: Yes, Lena will be the SE lead. She'll run the benchmark and be your point for infra questions.
[11:02] Lena Ortiz: I'll coordinate with Priya on networking and artifacts, and with Evan for the workload traces.
[11:07] Evan Park: Good. A few specific questions from product: can we do per-route model pinning so that trading routes use 13B and support routes use 7B?
[11:16] Lena Ortiz: Yes, route-level model pinning is supported; you can set quotas and concurrency at route level.
[11:22] Marisol Gomez: Do you have any customers in finance with similar needs?
[11:26] Samir Patel: Yes, a few financial services customers use Dedicated for low-latency trading and embeddings for research. We can share anonymized references.
[11:33] Priya Shah: Anything else on security posture? We need vulnerability scanning reports.
[11:38] Samir Patel: We'll include our penetration test summary and vulnerability management process in the security pack.
[11:44] Evan Park: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[11:46] Samir Patel: Recap: We'll send pricing + capacity plans (conservative vs cost-optimized), share SOC 2 and KMS docs, Lena will draft the benchmark plan, and we'll schedule a technical deep dive for the week of 11/23. Pilot target: 48-hour run.
[11:58] Marisol Gomez: Sounds good. Any blockers from procurement? Derek?
[12:02] Derek Liu: We'll review DPA and security annex and get back with any redlines.
[12:07] Priya Shah: I'll share the network diagram and access details by end of Thursday.
[12:12] Evan Park: We'll also prepare model artifacts and traces, hope to get them to you by Friday.
[12:18] Samir Patel: Great, I'll follow up with an email that includes the attachments and proposed time slots for the deep dive.
[12:24] Marisol Gomez: Thanks everyone.
[12:26] Samir Patel: Thanks — talk soon.
[50:00] Meeting end.
